originalTitle: WSL brings back Sunday evening kick-offs after indifferent viewing figures
summary: The move is part of an overhaul of its broadcast strategy after Sunday evening kick-offs were dropped last season after negative feedback from clubs and fans
content: The Women’s Super League will bring back Sunday evening kick-offs this season as part of an overhaul of its broadcast strategy after indifferent viewing figures last season. The Guardian has learned that the WSL will offer six different TV slots to broadcasters after releasing its fixtures for the 2026-27 campaign later on Thursday in a significant change from last season, when the majority of televised games took place on Saturday and Sunday lunchtimes. Sky Sports, which has the live rights for 163 of the WSL’s 182 games, retains the Saturday 12.45pm slot and noon on Sundays, but has also been given new regular kick-off times of 7pm on Friday and 6pm on Sunday. The BBC will broadcast 19 matches live at 12.30pm on Saturdays and 2.30pm on Sundays. The WSL’s new strategy is to spread games across the weekend after scheduling most fixtures at noon on Sundays last season, with multiple televised matches kicking off at the same time in a move that diluted the audience. The change this season follows a lengthy consultation with broadcasters, clubs and fans, with the WSL seeking a schedule that maximises its TV audience and matchday attendances. The Sunday evening kick-off was dropped last season after negative feedback from clubs and fans, as attendances were generally poor, but it was popular with broadcasters and was Sky’s best performing slot in 2024-25 with an average audience of 144,000. In an attempt to balance these competing interests, the Sunday evening game will mostly be brought forward 45 minutes to 6pm – with some changes likely to avoid clashes with the 4.30pm Premier League games – while the WSL will attempt to schedule derbies for that slot and Friday evenings where possible. The Guardian revealed last December that the WSL was considering further changes to its kick-off times this season after concern from Sky in particular at some of their viewing figures for lunchtime games. An average audience of 59,000 watched Sky’s live coverage of Arsenal’s home win over Liverpool that month, even fewer than the 71,000 people who watched Arsenal v Chelsea on Sky in the same noon kick-off slot the previous month. As well as struggling to attract a casual audience the decision to schedule up to four of the six weekly matches at the same time proved unpopular with the most committed WSL fans, who were unable to watch multiple matches live. Sky are paying the vast majority of the joint £65m broadcast deal with the BBC, who are believed to contribute around £8m in rights fees, so have a significant say but the WSL has consulted widely.
chineseTitle: 在收视率低迷后，WSL 恢复周日晚上的开球
chineseSummary: 上赛季因俱乐部和球迷的负面反馈而取消了周日晚上的开球，此举是其转播策略改革的一部分
chineseContent: 继上赛季收视率低迷后，女足超级联赛将在本赛季恢复周日晚上的开球，作为其转播策略改革的一部分。 《卫报》获悉，WSL 将在周四晚些时候发布 2026-27 赛季的赛程后，向广播公司提供六种不同的电视时段，这与上赛季相比有重大变化，当时大多数电视转播的比赛都在周六和周日的午餐时间进行。天空体育拥有 WSL 182 场比赛中 163 场比赛的直播权，保留了周六下午 12.45 分和周日中午的比赛时间，但也获得了新的常规开球时间，即周五晚上 7 点和周日下午 6 点。 BBC 将在周六中午 12.30 和周日下午 2.30 直播 19 场比赛。 WSL的新策略是在上赛季将大部分比赛安排在周日中午之后，将比赛分散到周末，多场电视转播的比赛同时开始，此举分散了观众的注意力。本赛季的改变是在与广播公司、俱乐部和球迷进行了长时间的协商之后做出的，WSL寻求一个能够最大限度地提高电视观众和比赛日上座率的时间表。上赛季，由于上座率普遍较低，俱乐部和球迷给出了负面反馈，周日晚上的开球被取消，但它很受广播公司的欢迎，是天空电视台 2024-25 赛季表现最好的时段，平均观众人数为 144,000 人。为了平衡这些相互竞争的利益，周日晚上的比赛将大部分提前 45 分钟至下午 6 点——进行一些更改可能是为了避免与下午 4.30 的英超比赛发生冲突——而 WSL 将尝试在该时段和周五晚上安排德比（如果可能）。 《卫报》去年 12 月透露，WSL 正在考虑进一步改变 i
